front: Recognizing pediatric rhythms: Complete: ________ determines the urgency of arrhythmia management.
explanation: Hemodynamic stability determines the urgency of arrhythmia management.

front: Recognizing pediatric rhythms: Complete: ________ often reflects an underlying cause such as fever, pain, or hypovolemia.
explanation: Sinus tachycardia often reflects an underlying cause such as fever, pain, or hypovolemia.

front: Pneumonia in children: Complete: ________ is infection of lung parenchyma and may cause fever, cough, tachypnea, and increased work of breathing.
explanation: Pneumonia is infection of lung parenchyma and may cause fever, cough, tachypnea, and increased work of breathing.

front: Pneumonia in children: Complete: ________ and respiratory distress are important severity findings.
explanation: Hypoxemia and respiratory distress are important severity findings.

front: Bronchiolitis fundamentals: Complete: ________ is a viral lower-airway illness affecting small airways in infants and young children.
explanation: Bronchiolitis is a viral lower-airway illness affecting small airways in infants and young children.

front: Bronchiolitis fundamentals: Complete: ________ is a common cause, although other viruses also produce bronchiolitis.
explanation: Respiratory syncytial virus is a common cause, although other viruses also produce bronchiolitis.

front: Peritonsillar infection: Complete: ________ is a collection of pus adjacent to the tonsil.
explanation: Peritonsillar abscess is a collection of pus adjacent to the tonsil.

front: Peritonsillar infection: Complete: ________ and a muffled voice support the diagnosis in the appropriate setting.
explanation: Trismus and a muffled voice support the diagnosis in the appropriate setting.

front: Deep neck space infection: Complete: ________ may cause fever, neck stiffness, dysphagia, and airway symptoms.
explanation: Retropharyngeal infection may cause fever, neck stiffness, dysphagia, and airway symptoms.

front: Deep neck space infection: Complete: ________ may help define a deep neck collection when the airway is stable and imaging is appropriate.
explanation: Contrast-enhanced CT may help define a deep neck collection when the airway is stable and imaging is appropriate.

front: Bacterial tracheitis: Complete: ________ can cause severe upper-airway obstruction through inflammation and thick secretions.
explanation: Bacterial tracheitis can cause severe upper-airway obstruction through inflammation and thick secretions.

front: Bacterial tracheitis: Complete: ________ is a recognized causative organism.
explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is a recognized causative organism.

front: Epiglottitis recognition: Complete: ________ is inflammation of supraglottic structures that can rapidly obstruct the airway.
explanation: Epiglottitis is inflammation of supraglottic structures that can rapidly obstruct the airway.

front: Epiglottitis recognition: Complete: ________ and difficulty swallowing are important clinical clues.
explanation: Drooling and difficulty swallowing are important clinical clues.

front: Croup recognition: Complete: ________ is a key mechanism in croup.
explanation: Subglottic edema is a key mechanism in croup.

front: Croup recognition: Complete: ________ and inspiratory stridor are characteristic clinical findings.
explanation: Barking cough and inspiratory stridor are characteristic clinical findings.

front: Junctional rhythms: Complete: ________ tissue can act as an escape pacemaker when sinus impulses fail or are not conducted.
explanation: AV junction tissue can act as an escape pacemaker when sinus impulses fail or are not conducted.

front: Junctional rhythms: Complete: ________ may appear before, within, or after the QRS complex.
explanation: Retrograde P waves may appear before, within, or after the QRS complex.

front: Sinus bradycardia: Complete: ________ has a sinus P wave before each QRS with a slower-than-expected heart rate.
explanation: Sinus bradycardia has a sinus P wave before each QRS with a slower-than-expected heart rate.

front: Sinus bradycardia: Complete: ________ and sleep can produce physiologic slowing.
explanation: Athletic conditioning and sleep can produce physiologic slowing.

front: Ventricular ectopy: Complete: ________ originate in ventricular tissue before the next expected sinus beat.
explanation: Premature ventricular contractions originate in ventricular tissue before the next expected sinus beat.

front: Ventricular ectopy: Complete: ________ are typical because activation does not follow the usual ventricular conduction sequence.
explanation: Wide QRS complexes are typical because activation does not follow the usual ventricular conduction sequence.

front: Rapid sequence intubation concepts: Complete: ________ increases the oxygen reserve before induction and apnea.
explanation: Preoxygenation increases the oxygen reserve before induction and apnea.

front: Rapid sequence intubation concepts: Complete: ________ facilitates intubation but does not provide sedation or analgesia.
explanation: Neuromuscular blockade facilitates intubation but does not provide sedation or analgesia.

front: Atrial ectopy: Complete: ________ arise from an atrial focus outside the sinus node.
explanation: Premature atrial contractions arise from an atrial focus outside the sinus node.

front: Atrial ectopy: Complete: ________ can distinguish an ectopic atrial beat from a sinus beat.
explanation: Abnormal P-wave morphology can distinguish an ectopic atrial beat from a sinus beat.

front: Extraglottic airway devices: Complete: ________ establish a ventilatory pathway above the vocal cords.
explanation: Supraglottic devices establish a ventilatory pathway above the vocal cords.

front: Extraglottic airway devices: Complete: ________ is an important role when mask ventilation or tracheal intubation is difficult.
explanation: Rescue ventilation is an important role when mask ventilation or tracheal intubation is difficult.

front: Spinal motion restriction: Complete: ________ aims to limit additional movement when spinal injury is suspected.
explanation: Motion restriction aims to limit additional movement when spinal injury is suspected.

front: Spinal motion restriction: Complete: ________ documents motor and sensory function before and after movement when possible.
explanation: Neurologic examination documents motor and sensory function before and after movement when possible.

front: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia: Complete: ________ is cyclic variation in sinus rate with breathing.
explanation: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia is cyclic variation in sinus rate with breathing.

front: Respiratory sinus arrhythmia: Complete: ________ commonly increases heart rate while expiration slows it.
explanation: Inspiration commonly increases heart rate while expiration slows it.

front: Bag-mask ventilation concepts: Complete: ________ is essential to limit leak during assisted ventilation.
explanation: Mask seal is essential to limit leak during assisted ventilation.

front: Bag-mask ventilation concepts: Complete: ________ improves patency and the delivery of breaths.
explanation: Airway positioning improves patency and the delivery of breaths.

front: Noninvasive positive pressure: Complete: ________ applies a continuous positive airway pressure throughout the respiratory cycle.
explanation: CPAP applies a continuous positive airway pressure throughout the respiratory cycle.

front: Noninvasive positive pressure: Complete: ________ provides different inspiratory and expiratory pressures.
explanation: Bilevel ventilation provides different inspiratory and expiratory pressures.

front: Airway assessment and patency: Complete: ________ can obstruct the upper airway in an unconscious person.
explanation: Tongue displacement can obstruct the upper airway in an unconscious person.

front: Airway assessment and patency: Complete: ________ can help open the airway when cervical motion should be minimized.
explanation: Jaw thrust can help open the airway when cervical motion should be minimized.

front: During bedside airway assessment, what does gurgling suggest?
back: Liquid or secretions in the upper airway.
explanation: Blood, vomit or secretions can produce gurgling as air passes through them. Assess patency and the ability to clear or protect the airway promptly.

references.title: Stabilization of the acutely ill patient — SAEM

front: What does inspiratory stridor suggest during an airway assessment?
explanation: Turbulent airflow through a narrowed upper airway produces this sound. Acute stridor with distress requires urgent assessment.

references.title: Stabilization of the acutely ill patient — SAEM

front: Does an inability to speak always establish airway obstruction?
back: No. Altered consciousness or impaired language function can also prevent speech.
explanation: Combine speech with breathing effort, airflow, airway sounds and examination; a single observation does not establish airway patency.

references.title: Stabilization of the acutely ill patient — SAEM

front: What can crepitus in the neck or upper chest indicate during resuscitation?
back: Air in the soft tissues, potentially from pneumothorax or tracheolaryngeal injury.
explanation: This finding should prompt evaluation for the underlying injury rather than being treated as proof of uncomplicated airway patency.

references.title: Stabilization of the acutely ill patient — SAEM

front: Hepatic encephalopathy: Complete: ________ is brain dysfunction associated with liver insufficiency or portosystemic shunting.
explanation: Hepatic encephalopathy is brain dysfunction associated with liver insufficiency or portosystemic shunting.

front: Hepatic encephalopathy: Complete: ________ is a possible examination finding but is not specific to this condition.
explanation: Asterixis is a possible examination finding but is not specific to this condition.

front: Gastroesophageal reflux: Complete: ________ permits gastric contents to reflux into the esophagus.
explanation: Lower esophageal sphincter dysfunction permits gastric contents to reflux into the esophagus.

front: Gastroesophageal reflux: Complete: ________ and regurgitation are typical symptoms.
explanation: Heartburn and regurgitation are typical symptoms.

front: H. pylori treatment principles: Complete: ________ is a key determinant of eradication regimen selection.
explanation: Antibiotic resistance is a key determinant of eradication regimen selection.

front: H. pylori treatment principles: Complete: ________ is a recommended empiric option in the ACG 2024 guidance when susceptibility is unknown.
explanation: Bismuth quadruple therapy is a recommended empiric option in the ACG 2024 guidance when susceptibility is unknown.

front: Bismuth subsalicylate: Complete: ________ contributes local protective and antimicrobial effects in the gastrointestinal tract.
explanation: Bismuth contributes local protective and antimicrobial effects in the gastrointestinal tract.

front: Bismuth subsalicylate: Complete: ________ exposure is relevant to allergy, interactions, and toxicity risk.
explanation: Salicylate exposure is relevant to allergy, interactions, and toxicity risk.

front: Peptic ulcer disease foundations: Complete: ________ infection and NSAID exposure are major causes of peptic ulcer disease.
explanation: H. pylori infection and NSAID exposure are major causes of peptic ulcer disease.

front: Peptic ulcer disease foundations: Complete: ________ penetration distinguishes an ulcer from a more superficial erosion.
explanation: Muscularis mucosae penetration distinguishes an ulcer from a more superficial erosion.

front: Oxygen therapy principles: Complete: ________ refers to oxygen transfer into blood and is distinct from carbon dioxide clearance.
explanation: Oxygenation refers to oxygen transfer into blood and is distinct from carbon dioxide clearance.

front: Oxygen therapy principles: Complete: ________ estimates arterial oxygen saturation but does not directly measure ventilation.
explanation: Pulse oximetry estimates arterial oxygen saturation but does not directly measure ventilation.

front: Asthma: inflammation and variable airflow: Complete: ________ is a defining physiologic feature of asthma.
explanation: Variable expiratory airflow limitation is a defining physiologic feature of asthma.

front: Asthma: inflammation and variable airflow: Complete: ________ reduces exacerbation risk and is central to current GINA management.
explanation: Inhaled corticosteroid-containing treatment reduces exacerbation risk and is central to current GINA management.

front: Before stepping up asthma medication, which two medication-use problems should be checked?
back: Incorrect inhaler technique and poor adherence.
explanation: An ineffective delivery technique or missed controller doses can mimic treatment failure. GINA advises checking these before increasing treatment intensity.

front: In asthma care, what does maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART) mean?
back: The prescribed ICS-formoterol inhaler is used for both scheduled maintenance and symptom relief.
explanation: Formoterol has a rapid onset. This approach uses an appropriate ICS-formoterol regimen; it is not interchangeable with every ICS-LABA combination.

front: Anti-IL-5 therapy: Complete: ________ supports eosinophil growth and survival.
explanation: Interleukin-5 supports eosinophil growth and survival.

front: Anti-IL-5 therapy: Complete: ________ and reslizumab target IL-5 in selected patients with severe eosinophilic asthma.
explanation: Mepolizumab and reslizumab target IL-5 in selected patients with severe eosinophilic asthma.

front: Omalizumab: Complete: ________ is the target of omalizumab.
explanation: IgE is the target of omalizumab.

front: Omalizumab: Complete: ________ is an established indication in appropriately selected patients.
explanation: Allergic asthma is an established indication in appropriately selected patients.

front: Leukotriene modifiers: Complete: ________ blocks the cysteinyl leukotriene receptor.
explanation: Montelukast blocks the cysteinyl leukotriene receptor.

front: Leukotriene modifiers: Complete: ________ inhibits 5-lipoxygenase and reduces leukotriene synthesis.
explanation: Zileuton inhibits 5-lipoxygenase and reduces leukotriene synthesis.

front: Inhaled corticosteroids: Complete: ________ is reduced by inhaled corticosteroids.
explanation: Airway inflammation is reduced by inhaled corticosteroids.

front: Inhaled corticosteroids: Complete: ________ is a local adverse effect.
explanation: Oral candidiasis is a local adverse effect.

front: Methylxanthines: Complete: ________ has bronchodilator activity and a narrow therapeutic index.
explanation: Theophylline has bronchodilator activity and a narrow therapeutic index.

front: Methylxanthines: Complete: ________ can significantly alter theophylline concentrations.
explanation: Drug interactions can significantly alter theophylline concentrations.

front: Ipratropium: Complete: ________ reduces vagally mediated bronchoconstriction.
explanation: Muscarinic receptor blockade reduces vagally mediated bronchoconstriction.

front: Ipratropium: Complete: ________ is a short-acting inhaled antimuscarinic.
explanation: Ipratropium is a short-acting inhaled antimuscarinic.

front: Beta-2 agonists: Complete: ________ relaxes bronchial smooth muscle.
explanation: Beta-2 receptor stimulation relaxes bronchial smooth muscle.

front: Beta-2 agonists: Complete: ________ is an intracellular mediator of the bronchodilator response.
explanation: Cyclic AMP is an intracellular mediator of the bronchodilator response.

front: Which pattern of respiratory symptoms supports an asthma diagnosis?
back: Symptoms that vary over time and intensity, often worsening at night or with triggers.
explanation: Episodic wheeze, breathlessness, chest tightness or cough supports the clinical suspicion; objective evidence of variable expiratory airflow is also sought.

front: Does a normal chest examination between episodes rule out asthma?
back: No. The examination can be normal between symptomatic episodes.
explanation: Asthma is variable. History and objective testing are needed; the absence of wheeze at a single visit does not exclude it.

front: NSAID pharmacology: Complete: ________ reduces prostaglandin production.
explanation: Cyclooxygenase inhibition reduces prostaglandin production.

front: NSAID pharmacology: Complete: ________ and reduction of inflammation are major therapeutic effects.
explanation: Analgesia and reduction of inflammation are major therapeutic effects.

front: Sternoclavicular joint injury: Complete: ________ can threaten mediastinal structures.
explanation: Posterior displacement can threaten mediastinal structures.

front: Sternoclavicular joint injury: Complete: ________ is useful for defining the direction and extent of displacement.
explanation: CT imaging is useful for defining the direction and extent of displacement.

front: Which ligaments are disrupted in a Rockwood type III acromioclavicular injury?
explanation: The classification reflects the pattern and degree of displacement, not just pain severity.

front: What distinguishes a Rockwood type IV acromioclavicular injury?
back: Posterior displacement of the distal clavicle into or through the trapezius.
explanation: Axillary imaging helps identify posterior displacement that an AP view may miss.

front: What minimum duration is required for the symptom cluster of a major depressive episode?
explanation: Duration alone is insufficient: symptom count, impairment, exclusions and a mood history must also be assessed.

front: Which core symptom must be present in a major depressive episode?
back: Depressed mood or loss of interest or pleasure.
explanation: Other symptoms alone do not establish the episode; assess functional impact and possible manic or hypomanic episodes.

front: Omphalocele: Complete: ________ at the umbilicus allows herniation of abdominal contents.
explanation: Midline abdominal wall defect at the umbilicus allows herniation of abdominal contents.

front: Omphalocele: Complete: ________ usually covers the herniated organs in omphalocele.
explanation: Membranous sac usually covers the herniated organs in omphalocele.

front: Seizure classification: Complete: ________ indicates a seizure beginning within networks in one hemisphere.
explanation: Focal onset indicates a seizure beginning within networks in one hemisphere.

front: Seizure classification: Complete: ________ involves bilateral networks from the start.
explanation: Generalized onset involves bilateral networks from the start.

front: Abdominal wall anatomy: Complete: ________ is the most superficial of the three lateral flat abdominal muscles.
explanation: External oblique is the most superficial of the three lateral flat abdominal muscles.

front: Abdominal wall anatomy: Complete: ________ is the deepest of the three lateral muscle layers.
explanation: Transversus abdominis is the deepest of the three lateral muscle layers.

front: Gastroschisis: Complete: ________ is characteristic of gastroschisis, usually to the right of the umbilicus.
explanation: Paraumbilical defect is characteristic of gastroschisis, usually to the right of the umbilicus.

front: Gastroschisis: Complete: ________ lacks the membranous sac typical of omphalocele.
explanation: Exposed bowel lacks the membranous sac typical of omphalocele.

front: What pattern suggests neuroleptic malignant syndrome after dopamine blockade?
back: Fever, severe muscle rigidity, mental status change and autonomic instability.
explanation: This is a clinical emergency; the medication history is central to recognition.

front: Why can creatine kinase rise markedly in neuroleptic malignant syndrome?
back: Sustained muscle rigidity can cause rhabdomyolysis.
explanation: Muscle breakdown can contribute to acute kidney injury and electrolyte disturbances.

front: Meconium aspiration: Complete: ________ and chemical inflammation contribute to meconium aspiration syndrome.
explanation: Airway obstruction and chemical inflammation contribute to meconium aspiration syndrome.

front: Meconium aspiration: Complete: ________ can worsen respiratory mechanics.
explanation: Surfactant dysfunction can worsen respiratory mechanics.

front: Neonatal sepsis: Complete: ________ may include feeding difficulty, temperature instability, and respiratory distress.
explanation: Nonspecific signs may include feeding difficulty, temperature instability, and respiratory distress.

front: Neonatal sepsis: Complete: ________ help identify the pathogen when obtained appropriately.
explanation: Blood cultures help identify the pathogen when obtained appropriately.

front: Neonatal cyanosis: Complete: ________ reflects reduced arterial oxygenation or abnormal hemoglobin rather than isolated peripheral vasoconstriction.
explanation: Central cyanosis reflects reduced arterial oxygenation or abnormal hemoglobin rather than isolated peripheral vasoconstriction.

front: Neonatal cyanosis: Complete: ________ and pulmonary disease are major diagnostic categories.
explanation: Cardiac disease and pulmonary disease are major diagnostic categories.

front: Hernia evaluation: Complete: ________ can return through the defect into its usual compartment.
explanation: Reducible hernia can return through the defect into its usual compartment.

front: Hernia evaluation: Complete: ________ means the contents are trapped and cannot be reduced.
explanation: Incarceration means the contents are trapped and cannot be reduced.

front: Why may an inguinal hernia bulge become more noticeable with coughing or straining?
back: Increased intra-abdominal pressure pushes contents toward the abdominal-wall defect.
explanation: The bulge and discomfort may become more apparent when standing, coughing or straining, although a hernia can also be asymptomatic.

front: What makes a strangulated hernia more dangerous than incarceration alone?
back: The trapped tissue has a compromised blood supply.
explanation: Ischemia can injure the bowel. Severe pain or obstructive symptoms such as vomiting with a hernia require urgent assessment.

front: How does buprenorphine act at the mu-opioid receptor?
explanation: Its affinity allows it to displace full agonists, while its intrinsic activity is lower.

front: Why can buprenorphine precipitate withdrawal if started too soon after a full opioid agonist?
back: It displaces the full agonist but provides less receptor activation.
explanation: Initiation timing and protocol matter; the risk does not mean buprenorphine has no agonist activity.

front: Alcohol-associated hepatitis: Complete: ________ related to alcohol exposure can present with jaundice.
explanation: Inflammatory liver injury related to alcohol exposure can present with jaundice.

front: Alcohol-associated hepatitis: Complete: ________ over ALT is common but is not diagnostic by itself.
explanation: AST predominance over ALT is common but is not diagnostic by itself.

front: Acute liver failure: Complete: ________ and encephalopathy are central features of acute liver failure in the appropriate clinical setting.
explanation: Coagulopathy and encephalopathy are central features of acute liver failure in the appropriate clinical setting.

front: Acute liver failure: Complete: ________ is an important cause.
explanation: Acetaminophen toxicity is an important cause.

front: Which meperidine metabolite is associated with neurotoxicity and seizures?
explanation: Repeated exposure and impaired elimination can promote metabolite accumulation.

front: What is another name for pethidine?
explanation: Recognizing both names helps avoid duplicate opioid prescribing and medication-history errors.

front: Interpreting liver tests: Complete: ________ indicate hepatocellular injury rather than directly measuring liver function.
explanation: Aminotransferases indicate hepatocellular injury rather than directly measuring liver function.

front: Interpreting liver tests: Complete: ________ may rise in cholestasis but also has nonhepatic sources.
explanation: Alkaline phosphatase may rise in cholestasis but also has nonhepatic sources.

front: Estimating burn extent: Complete: ________ estimates generally include partial- and full-thickness burns, not simple superficial erythema.
explanation: Total body surface area estimates generally include partial- and full-thickness burns, not simple superficial erythema.

front: Estimating burn extent: Complete: ________ adjusts body proportions for age.
explanation: Lund-Browder chart adjusts body proportions for age.

front: Fourth-degree burns: Complete: ________ beyond skin into muscle, tendon, or bone defines this severe injury category.
explanation: Deep tissue extension beyond skin into muscle, tendon, or bone defines this severe injury category.

front: Fourth-degree burns: Complete: ________ must be assessed beyond the visible surface.
explanation: Tissue viability must be assessed beyond the visible surface.

front: Full-thickness burns: Complete: ________ destruction is characteristic of full-thickness burns.
explanation: Entire dermis destruction is characteristic of full-thickness burns.

front: Full-thickness burns: Complete: ________ may be present, with variable color.
explanation: Leathery appearance may be present, with variable color.

front: Partial-thickness burns: Complete: ________ distinguishes partial-thickness injury from a superficial epidermal burn.
explanation: Dermal involvement distinguishes partial-thickness injury from a superficial epidermal burn.

front: Partial-thickness burns: Complete: ________ is a common finding.
explanation: Blistering is a common finding.

front: Superficial burns: Complete: ________ is the main layer involved in a superficial burn.
explanation: Epidermis is the main layer involved in a superficial burn.

front: Superficial burns: Complete: ________ reflects increased blood flow in the affected skin.
explanation: Erythema reflects increased blood flow in the affected skin.

front: Intravenous fluid concepts: Complete: ________ contain small solutes that distribute within extracellular compartments according to their composition.
explanation: Crystalloids contain small solutes that distribute within extracellular compartments according to their composition.

front: Intravenous fluid concepts: Complete: ________ have electrolyte and buffer compositions designed to reduce chloride loading relative to saline.
explanation: Balanced solutions have electrolyte and buffer compositions designed to reduce chloride loading relative to saline.

front: Membranous nephropathy: Complete: ________ are a defining ultrastructural finding.
explanation: Subepithelial immune deposits are a defining ultrastructural finding.

front: Membranous nephropathy: Complete: ________ is a common presentation.
explanation: Nephrotic syndrome is a common presentation.

front: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis: Complete: ________ means some glomeruli are affected.
explanation: Focal means some glomeruli are affected.

front: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis: Complete: ________ means only part of an affected glomerulus is scarred.
explanation: Segmental means only part of an affected glomerulus is scarred.

front: Minimal change disease: Complete: ________ is the characteristic electron-microscopic finding.
explanation: Foot process effacement is the characteristic electron-microscopic finding.

front: Minimal change disease: Complete: ________ may show little or no obvious abnormality.
explanation: Light microscopy may show little or no obvious abnormality.

front: Nephrotic syndrome: Complete: ________ results from altered glomerular filtration barrier function.
explanation: Heavy proteinuria results from altered glomerular filtration barrier function.

front: Nephrotic syndrome: Complete: ________ contributes to edema.
explanation: Hypoalbuminemia contributes to edema.

front: Grafts and flaps: Complete: ________ are transferred without their own intact blood supply.
explanation: Skin grafts are transferred without their own intact blood supply.

front: Grafts and flaps: Complete: ________ retain or reestablish a vascular supply as part of transfer.
explanation: Flaps retain or reestablish a vascular supply as part of transfer.

front: Hypertrophic and keloid scars: Complete: ________ remain within the boundaries of the original wound.
explanation: Hypertrophic scars remain within the boundaries of the original wound.

front: Hypertrophic and keloid scars: Complete: ________ extend beyond the original injury margins.
explanation: Keloids extend beyond the original injury margins.

front: Infectious mononucleosis: Complete: ________ is the classic cause of infectious mononucleosis.
explanation: Epstein-Barr virus is the classic cause of infectious mononucleosis.

front: Infectious mononucleosis: Complete: ________ is a typical examination finding.
explanation: Posterior cervical lymphadenopathy is a typical examination finding.

front: Portal hypertension: Complete: ________ results from increased resistance, increased flow, or both.
explanation: Increased portal pressure results from increased resistance, increased flow, or both.

front: Portal hypertension: Complete: ________ is a common cause of intrahepatic resistance.
explanation: Cirrhosis is a common cause of intrahepatic resistance.

front: Pneumonia severity assessment: Complete: ________ incorporates confusion, urea, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and age.
explanation: CURB-65 incorporates confusion, urea, respiratory rate, blood pressure, and age.

front: Pneumonia severity assessment: Complete: ________ remains necessary because a score cannot capture every risk.
explanation: Clinical judgment remains necessary because a score cannot capture every risk.

front: Wound healing: Complete: ________ describes healing of closely approximated wound edges.
explanation: Primary intention describes healing of closely approximated wound edges.

front: Wound healing: Complete: ________ involves filling a larger tissue defect with granulation tissue and contraction.
explanation: Secondary intention involves filling a larger tissue defect with granulation tissue and contraction.

front: Water balance disorders: Complete: ________ causes impaired urinary concentration from deficient vasopressin action.
explanation: Diabetes insipidus causes impaired urinary concentration from deficient vasopressin action.

front: Water balance disorders: Complete: ________ produces inappropriate water retention and hypotonic hyponatremia in the appropriate setting.
explanation: SIADH produces inappropriate water retention and hypotonic hyponatremia in the appropriate setting.

front: Burkitt lymphoma: Complete: ________ is central to Burkitt lymphoma.
explanation: MYC dysregulation is central to Burkitt lymphoma.

front: Burkitt lymphoma: Complete: ________ results from macrophages scattered among rapidly proliferating tumor cells.
explanation: Starry-sky pattern results from macrophages scattered among rapidly proliferating tumor cells.

front: Pregnancy dating: Complete: ________ can provide an initial estimate when cycle dates are reliable.
explanation: Last menstrual period can provide an initial estimate when cycle dates are reliable.

front: Pregnancy dating: Complete: ________ is useful for establishing gestational age.
explanation: First-trimester ultrasound is useful for establishing gestational age.

front: Spinal cord injury classification: Complete: ________ evaluates key muscle groups systematically.
explanation: Motor testing evaluates key muscle groups systematically.

front: Spinal cord injury classification: Complete: ________ assesses light touch and pinprick in defined dermatomes.
explanation: Sensory testing assesses light touch and pinprick in defined dermatomes.

front: Serum-ascites albumin gradient: Complete: ________ is serum albumin minus ascitic fluid albumin, ideally measured close in time.
explanation: SAAG is serum albumin minus ascitic fluid albumin, ideally measured close in time.

front: Serum-ascites albumin gradient: Complete: ________ is suggested by a gradient of at least 1.1 g/dL in the appropriate setting.
explanation: Portal hypertension is suggested by a gradient of at least 1.1 g/dL in the appropriate setting.

front: Which pain finding raises concern for acute compartment syndrome?
back: Pain out of proportion to the injury, particularly with passive stretch.
explanation: Assessment is repeated over time; pain may be unreliable in an obtunded or insensate patient.

front: Do palpable distal pulses exclude acute compartment syndrome?
explanation: Microvascular tissue perfusion may be compromised while flow through larger arteries remains detectable.

front: What defines a degloving injury?
back: Separation of skin and subcutaneous tissue from the underlying fascia.
explanation: The shearing injury can disrupt blood supply and may be open or closed.

front: How does a hematoma differ from diffuse swelling?
back: A hematoma is a localized collection of blood outside vessels.
explanation: Diffuse swelling can include edema; the terms describe different tissue processes.

front: Receptor antagonists: Complete: ________ compete with agonists for the same binding site.
explanation: Competitive antagonists compete with agonists for the same binding site.

front: Receptor antagonists: Complete: ________ can be overcome by increasing agonist concentration.
explanation: Surmountable antagonism can be overcome by increasing agonist concentration.

front: Dose-response relationships: Complete: ________ describes the dose or concentration needed to produce a specified effect.
explanation: Potency describes the dose or concentration needed to produce a specified effect.

front: Dose-response relationships: Complete: ________ describes the maximum achievable effect.
explanation: Efficacy describes the maximum achievable effect.

front: Metronidazole: Complete: ________ of metronidazole damage microbial DNA.
explanation: Reactive metabolites of metronidazole damage microbial DNA.

front: Metronidazole: Complete: ________ are important targets.
explanation: Anaerobic organisms are important targets.

front: Fluoroquinolones: Complete: ________ and topoisomerase IV are bacterial enzyme targets.
explanation: DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV are bacterial enzyme targets.

front: Fluoroquinolones: Complete: ________ and levofloxacin are examples with differing spectra.
explanation: Ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin are examples with differing spectra.

front: Protein synthesis inhibitors: Complete: ________ provide targets distinct from mammalian cytoplasmic ribosomes.
explanation: Bacterial ribosomes provide targets distinct from mammalian cytoplasmic ribosomes.

front: Protein synthesis inhibitors: Complete: ________ inhibitors include aminoglycosides and tetracyclines.
explanation: 30S subunit inhibitors include aminoglycosides and tetracyclines.

front: Carbonic anhydrase inhibition: Complete: ________ inhibits carbonic anhydrase.
explanation: Acetazolamide inhibits carbonic anhydrase.

front: Carbonic anhydrase inhibition: Complete: ________ increases as proximal tubular reabsorption falls.
explanation: Bicarbonate excretion increases as proximal tubular reabsorption falls.

front: Celecoxib: Complete: ________ is relatively selective with celecoxib.
explanation: COX-2 inhibition is relatively selective with celecoxib.

front: Celecoxib: Complete: ________ results from reduced prostaglandin production.
explanation: Analgesic activity results from reduced prostaglandin production.

front: Sutures and needle handling: Complete: ________ lose tensile strength and are broken down over time.
explanation: Absorbable sutures lose tensile strength and are broken down over time.

front: Sutures and needle handling: Complete: ________ consist of a single strand.
explanation: Monofilament sutures consist of a single strand.

front: What is the swage of a surgical needle?
back: The junction where the suture is attached to the needle.
explanation: The swage is distinct from the needle body and tissue-penetrating point. Recognizing the components helps avoid damaging the attachment during handling.

front: Which part of a surgical needle determines whether its point is tapered, blunt or triangular?
explanation: Tip design influences how the needle enters tissue; the body and attachment are separate anatomical features of the instrument.

front: How are modern synthetic absorbable sutures generally broken down?
explanation: Water-mediated breakdown progressively reduces tensile strength and eventually allows absorption; this differs from the enzymatic degradation of natural gut.

front: Why must suture selection consider the rate at which the wound regains strength?
back: The suture must support the tissue through the required healing interval.
explanation: An absorbable material can lose useful tensile strength before it is fully absorbed. Material choice therefore depends on wound characteristics and the strength-retention profile.

front: Acute pancreatitis: Complete: ________ typically produces upper abdominal pain and may cause systemic illness.
explanation: Pancreatic inflammation typically produces upper abdominal pain and may cause systemic illness.

front: Acute pancreatitis: Complete: ________ supports the diagnosis in the appropriate context.
explanation: Lipase elevation supports the diagnosis in the appropriate context.

front: Acute appendicitis: Complete: ________ is a common finding.
explanation: Right lower quadrant tenderness is a common finding.

front: Acute appendicitis: Complete: ________ from a central location to the right lower quadrant can occur.
explanation: Pain migration from a central location to the right lower quadrant can occur.

front: Acute coronary syndromes: Complete: ________ occurs when oxygen supply is insufficient for myocardial demand.
explanation: Myocardial ischemia occurs when oxygen supply is insufficient for myocardial demand.

front: Acute coronary syndromes: Complete: ________ is an early essential investigation in suspected acute coronary syndrome.
explanation: ECG is an early essential investigation in suspected acute coronary syndrome.

front: Septic arthritis: Complete: ________ can rapidly damage articular cartilage.
explanation: Joint infection can rapidly damage articular cartilage.

front: Septic arthritis: Complete: ________ is central to evaluation when joint infection is suspected.
explanation: Synovial fluid analysis is central to evaluation when joint infection is suspected.

front: Acromioclavicular injury: Complete: ________ and coracoclavicular ligaments contribute to joint stability.
explanation: Acromioclavicular ligaments and coracoclavicular ligaments contribute to joint stability.

front: Acromioclavicular injury: Complete: ________ describes increasing and differing patterns of displacement and soft-tissue injury.
explanation: Rockwood classification describes increasing and differing patterns of displacement and soft-tissue injury.

front: Glasgow Coma Scale: Complete: ________ is one of the three GCS components.
explanation: Eye opening is one of the three GCS components.

front: Glasgow Coma Scale: Complete: ________ is assessed alongside eye and motor responses.
explanation: Verbal response is assessed alongside eye and motor responses.

front: When driving a curved surgical needle, how should the hand move it through tissue?
back: Rotate the wrist so the needle follows its own curvature.
explanation: A controlled arc follows the needle geometry; forcing it straight through can create unnecessary tissue trauma or bend the needle.

front: Where should the needle holder generally grasp a curved suture needle?
back: On the body, approximately one-third of the distance from the swaged end.
explanation: Grasping the body preserves the point and attachment while providing control. Needle and holder size must be appropriate for each other.
